sec: TFT overview, screening and binding-protein effects

items.q: Match the following TFT indications to the source's classification — 1) Universal neonatal screen 2) Routine community screening in adults 3) High-yield targeted screen … A) All newborns B) Not recommended routinely C) Symptomatic / high-risk groups
items.exp: The page recommends universal neonatal screening, advises against routine adult screening, and reserves tests for symptomatic or at-risk groups. (Book p902)

items.q: A healthy 30-year-old has a free-T4 normal but total T4 elevated. Pregnancy is excluded and she is on combined oral contraceptive pills. The most consistent pattern is:
opts: Increased TBG with normal free hormone
Increased TSH with low free T4
Low TBG with normal free T4
items.exp: OCPs raise TBG; total T4/T3 rise with free hormone and TSH normal. This must be distinguished from the rare FDHS where albumin binds excess T4. (Book p902)

items.q: Assess these TBG-effect statements: I Estrogen, pregnancy and chronic active hepatitis raise TBG. II Nephrotic syndrome lowers TBG.
items.exp: OCPs, estrogen, pregnancy, steroid therapy and chronic active hepatitis raise TBG; nephrotic syndrome, androgen and chronic liver disease lower TBG. (Book p902)

items.q: Match the following TBG change to its source — 1) ↑TBG 2) ↓TBG … A) Nephrotic syndrome B) Combined oral contraceptive pill
items.exp: The source lists OCPs, pregnancy, steroids and chronic active hepatitis under TBG excess, and nephrotic syndrome with protein-losing states under TBG deficit. (Book p902)

items.q: A patient on chronic glucocorticoids for SLE has normal free T4 and TSH, but total T4 is high. The biochemical mechanism is:
opts: Antibody-bound T4 with low free hormone
items.exp: Corticosteroids raise TBG and therefore raise total T4/T3 while free hormones and TSH remain normal. (Book p902)

items.q: Which condition is the odd one out compared with the others as a cause of raised TBG on this page?
items.exp: Nephrotic syndrome lowers TBG; estrogen, pregnancy and chronic active hepatitis all raise TBG per the source. (Book p902)

items.q: The most abundant thyroid-hormone transport protein on this page is ___, binding approximately two-thirds of circulating T4.
items.exp: TBG carries the largest fraction of T4 and T3; prealbumin and albumin bind smaller portions. (Book p902)

items.q: Evaluate these source statements on neonatal screening: I It is universally recommended for all newborns. II It targets congenital hypothyroidism to prevent cretinism.
items.exp: Universal newborn screening is standard practice because early levothyroxine prevents neurodevelopmental cretinism. (Book p902)

items.q: Match the following drugs / states to their TBG effect — 1) Androgen 2) Chronic liver disease 3) Oestrogen therapy 4) Nephrotic syndrome … A) ↑TBG B) ↓TBG
items.exp: Androgen, chronic liver disease and nephrotic syndrome all lower TBG; only oestrogen therapy raises it. (Book p902)

items.q: A laboratory reports normal free T4 with high total T4 in a clinically euthyroid patient on OCPs. What is the correct clinical action?
opts: No treatment — interpret total T4 in light of TBG change
Start levothyroxine because total T4 is high
Start methimazole because total T4 is high
Repeat total T4 only after stopping OCPs
items.exp: Free hormone and TSH are normal; the high total T4 reflects raised TBG from estrogen, not true hyperthyroidism. (Book p902)

items.q: Per the source, the binding protein transporting the largest fraction of circulating thyroid hormone is:
items.exp: TBG carries the majority of T4 and T3; prealbumin and albumin take much smaller fractions. (Book p902)

items.q: Assess the printed TBG list: I The source inherits (rare) as a TBG-excess cause. II Inherited deficiency is listed separately from nephrotic syndrome.
items.exp: The page lists inherited (rare) as a separate TBG-excess cause and inherited deficiency as a separate TBG-deficit cause from acquired nephrotic losses. (Book p902)
